document_title: Redwood Private Deployment: Upgrade and Rollback Procedure & Support Guidance
scope: Provides standard operational guidance for private cloud deployments utilizing Redwood Private, covering required prerequisites, supported upgrade paths, and defined support coverage commitments.
knowledge_points: Supported Upgrade Paths: Redwood Private supports in-place upgrades following a defined major version path (N-1 to N). Skipping major versions requires pre-approval via a Service Review Board.
Rollback Procedure: Rollback is supported after an upgrade failure, provided specific prerequisites are met.

Rollback Steps: 1) Verify pre-upgrade snapshot integrity of control-plane DB and config state. 2) If failure pre-migration, roll back application components. 3) If failure post-migration, restore DB from pre-upgrade snapshot (PITR or volume snapshot).

Rollback Caveats: Service restoration time is typically tens of minutes, depending on the storage backend (e.g., Managed DB PITR size vs. EBS/CSI recovery). Rollback is invalidated by non-reversible schema boundaries.
Support Coverage: Redwood Inference offers escalated support for planned private deployments, subject to meeting prerequisites.
Support Commitment: We commit to dedicated SRE/Release Engineering bridge coverage during the defined maintenance window.
Prerequisites for Support: Customer must share target version and precheck outputs 48 hours prior. A rollback drill in non-production must be documented. Window must be formally confirmed.
Support Response: A live support bridge will be established at the start of the window, ensuring continuous coverage until completion or rollback is confirmed.
Compliance: Redwood provides comprehensive reporting for all upgrade operations to meet regulatory requirements.
Audit Artifacts: Provided items include an Upgrade Report (precheck results, backup timestamps) and Audit Log Entries (upgrade start/stop, rollback invocation, depending on the Private version).
